cells.tense: You're here with the pen, deciding as things move, and the deciding isn't costing you anything.
cells.verb: cutting through the drag and getting things moving with your own hands on the wheel
cells.place: the place where you hold what has to be held and shape it while you carry it
cells.ask: offer one thing you're sure about to someone who's still forming their own answer — let what comes back be theirs, and let the comfort of not-knowing be part of what you carry forward. What comes back is structure that serves what it organizes: things make sense in your presence.
cells.core: You set the direction and move on it, and the moving doesn't crack you. You can charge forward and still hold what matters — not by stiffening against it, but by knowing what you're carrying and why. That's the seed of leadership: authority that's yours because you're willing to hold the weight of the call, not just make it.
cells.sheetLine: You decide and move, and you can hold the weight of that.

cells.tense: You're out ahead of the moment, acting for a version of events that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.verb: pushing the call twice as fast as the ground can take it
cells.place: the place where holding has turned into bracing — grip tight, weight not yet here
cells.ask: pull back and let the map form in your mind before you make it real — let one call go unmade for now, and let understanding from the ground catch up to what you already know. What comes back is structure that serves what it organizes: things make sense in your presence.
cells.core: You're leading into a future that hasn't happened yet. Every move is anticipatory, every boundary set in advance of the thing it's meant to bound — and the endurance you're spending is on weight that isn't here yet. The push is real; the moment it's meant for isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're making the call before the situation has asked for it.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a call you didn't make, and the moment for it has already passed.
cells.verb: holding the weight but not giving it a direction to go
cells.place: the place where endurance turned into standing still — holding form without moving it
cells.ask: start something small that has to change and let yourself be slow and unstoppable about it — one structural move you've been circling, not a leap but a beginning. What comes back is structure that serves what it organizes: things make sense in your presence.
cells.core: You can hold, and you're doing that part fine. What's missing is the charge — the moment where the holding becomes a direction. Somewhere back there, moving on your own read didn't go well, and you've been carrying without spending ever since. The capacity is intact. The ignition is what's missing.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying the weight but not spending it.

cells.tense: You're already leading in the room, already setting the direction, and calling it something other than your call.
cells.verb: moving things forward by momentum you're not claiming as yours
cells.place: the place where you hold what must be held — and don't say you're the one holding it
cells.ask: notice one thing you've been calling 'what needed to happen' and say out loud that it was your call — let one ending be named as yours, and let the renewal come from that honesty. What comes back is structure that serves what it organizes: things make sense in your presence.
cells.core: The leadership is running — people are following, the direction is being set, boundaries are being drawn — and you talk about it like it's the situation doing it. The charge is yours, the call is yours, and the one person who hasn't claimed it is you. Nothing needs to change about what you're doing; only about whose name is on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already leading. You just haven't said so.
